exposure: training intervention to arrest the decline in forceps competency
outcome: Rates of attempted and successful instrumental births
cohort: 72,490 births at Monash Health from 2005 to 2014, of which 8,789 (12%) were attempted instrumental vaginal births
finding: A policy of ensuring obstetric forceps competency before beginning vacuum training results in more forceps births, fewer postpartum hemorrhages, and no increase in third- and fourth-degree perineal injuries or episiotomies.
mod_finding: After the intervention, rates of forceps births increased, and vacuum births decreased.
